acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust ToolsForm owns selected tools page, shortcut recording, committed normalized history/timeline queries, history pagination and loaded state. Native platform/service adapters project that state into the existing Rust/Metal controls and retain visibility/profile/workspace/generation authorization and domain operations.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: The opt-in backend reads/writes the Rust ToolsForm instead of its legacy Views page/recording/query/limit/loaded members. Views retains native state and normal operation; rebuilding a page clears query, loaded and recorder state. Detach clears transient state; page identity is preserved by reset.

Committed history text is trimmed by the native Unicode service; timeline text is lowercased there. Rust stores exact UTF-16 units including partial surrogates. IME composing notifications remain excluded by the native adapter, so delayed history requests retain the committed query during preedit.

A fresh history request resets the limit to 200; More adds 200 with saturation in Rust. Request/edit marks unloaded. Rust admits matching query/limit and marks loaded, including completed error responses. Native visibility/current-profile checks run first. No new service request identity or stricter duplicate-response policy is claimed.

Shortcut recording state is in Rust; native accelerator reservation/registration and editor read-only/IME handling remain. Page selection retains native clamp to 0..3. Native posted-action generation/workspace/profile admission remains unchanged.

The new shared browser case covers completed history errors, wrong query/limit/profile responses, pending Unicode query edits and whitespace normalization, valid replacement, hidden-page rejection, clamped page selection and query reset on reconstruction. Existing real 205-row pagination, committed-query/preedit, timeline identity/filtering, shortcut Cocoa capture/cancellation, provider/actions and Metal scene/cutout cases remain in the critical gate.
No rendering recipe, crate/library/dependency, browser store or service authority is introduced or replaced by this change.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun in this controller checkpoint; the previous checkpoint retains its four default-30-trial passes per backend. No inherited result is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Tools action/status presentation decisions, provider/shortcut domain editing coordination, native history result rows/list, busy state and other form/service UI remain to migrate. Rust ToolsForm does not own stores, confirmations, service operations or native window/IME/menu/AX.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, complex bidi/RTL, typography/scale, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
